messages.author: c4ad98ee09d9ee51
messages.subject: error bar troubles
parts:
Hey all,

I'm just getting going using R and ggplot and I've run into a problem
using error bars.

For my plot I'm using:

Graph <- ggplot() +
+ layer (
+ data = DF, mapping = aes(x = V, y= -BV),
+ geom = "point", stat = "identity") +
+ scale_y_continuous("B-V", limits = c(-0.6, -0.2)) +
+ scale_x_continuous("V Magnitude", limits = c(11, 14)) +
+ coord_cartesian()

And everything turns out fine. To add error bars I'm doing:

Graph + geom_errorbar(aes(ymax = BV + BVerror, ymin = BV - BVerror))

Which gives me this error message:

"Error in eval(expr, envir, enclos) : object 'x' not found
In addition: Warning messages:
1: In BV + BVerror :
longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
2: In BV - BVerror :
longer object length is not a multiple of shorter object length
3: In min(diff(sort(x))) : no non-missing arguments to min; returning
Inf"

I'm not sure what this means or how to fix it.

I tried:

G <- qplot(V, BV)
G + geom_errorbar(aes(ymax = BV + BVerror, ymin = BV - BVerror))

This worked which confuses me even more. Why would it work with the
qplot shortcut and not ggplot?

messages.author: 5196f936ff792c35
messages.subject: Re: error bar troubles
parts:
It looks to me like you're defining a layer in your call, which then specifies the aes() for that specific layer. I think when you are adding your errorbars that the aes() call in your layer() calls are not transfered over and therefore you are not defining an x coordinate to plot them against. Without any data it's hard to play though. 

Try the following and see if it works. 

ggplot(data = DF, aes(x = V, y= -BV)) +
layer (geom = "point", stat = "identity") +
scale_y_continuous("B-V", limits = c(-0.6, -0.2)) +
scale_x_continuous("V Magnitude", limits = c(11, 14)) +
coord_cartesian()+
geom_errorbar(aes(ymax = BV + BVerror, ymin = BV - BVerror))
Brandon

messages.subject: Re: error bar troubles
parts:
Alexa, 

I put together some code to make up some data to fit your problem. Not sure if it's close enough, but I had to tweak your code to get it to work. 

#Load required packages 
require(plotrix)
require(ggplot2)

#makes a dataframe of 25 points, computes SEM for "BV" and outputs to third column
DF<-cbind(runif(25, min=-0.5, max=-0.2), runif(25, min=11.1, max=13.9))
DF<-as.data.frame(DF)
colnames(DF)[1]<-"BV"
colnames(DF)[2]<-"V"
DF[[3]]<-std.error(DF[[1]])
colnames(DF)[3]<-"BVerror"

#Shows the dataframe
DF

#Initiate plot, notice I changed the y= -BV to y=BV and got rid of the layer call
Graph <- ggplot(data = DF, aes(x = V, y = BV))+
geom_point() +

scale_y_continuous("B-V", limits = c(-0.6, -0.2)) +
scale_x_continuous("V Magnitude", limits = c(11, 14)) +
coord_cartesian()

Graph

Graph + 
geom_errorbar(aes(ymax = BV + BVerror, ymin = BV -
BVerror))

##########
Without your data it's really hard to say where things are going wrong exactly. I notice that you were flipping the BV values for plotting, but not doing so for the errorbar calculations. I'm also not sure why you even need the call for coord_cartesian(), when you are defining that your coordinates are cartesian with the scale_*_continuous() calls. If you can't get it to work after this, we'll have to hope someone who's been at this a lot longer than me can help you. 

HTH, 

Brandon
